learningObjective: Design a shape-coverage matrix for testing a GPU kernel so that the test suite covers boundary shapes, tile-boundary shapes, and typical production shapes.
stem: You are writing shape-coverage tests for a fused pointwise kernel with a compile-time tile size of 128. Which shape set is most likely to catch bugs before production?

options.text: Only power-of-two shapes: 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048. These are the most common in ML workloads; if the kernel works on power-of-two sizes it will work on all others by symmetry, so covering non-power-of-two is redundant.
Only very large shapes (≥ 10⁶ elements) to make sure the kernel utilizes the GPU; small shapes never expose bugs because they finish quickly, and testing them wastes CI time.

A matrix that includes: 0 (empty), 1 (singleton), tile-boundary sizes (127, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257), a couple of large production sizes, and a random-shape fuzz set. This covers boundary handling (mask logic), off-tile-multiple handling, and typical inputs.

The exact production shape set (e.g., `M=32, N=4096`), because tests should validate the actual deployment path. Covering other shapes wastes CI cycles and is not required if the kernel is only used with fixed shapes at inference time.

explanation: Kernel bugs commonly appear at boundaries: empty tensors, singletons, tile-boundary values (n = tile, n = tile+1, n = tile-1), and interactions between mask logic and the last tile. A well-designed shape matrix covers those edge cases plus a fuzz set. Options A/B/D miss important classes of bugs: A ignores mask logic for non-tile-multiples; B fails to exercise the edge cases; D is fragile against future changes to production shapes.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: mask logic bugs surface at non-power-of-two shapes.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: small shapes exercise edge cases that large shapes may bypass.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: boundary + production + fuzz coverage is the standard discipline.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: production shapes only make the test fragile to workload changes.

assumptions: Kernel has a compile-time tile size and uses masked loads/stores at tile boundaries.
nonImplications: Does not imply exhaustive shape coverage is needed; a well-chosen boundary set + fuzz is sufficient.
Does not imply CI time is unlimited; parameterized tests can prune redundant shapes.
